why.reputation.down: It goes down when you hire below the asked wage ({low}), refuse a raise ({raise}), let someone go in their first season ({probation}), can't pay a season's wages ({lapse}) or sell a bad batch ({batch}).
why.reputation.high: At {high} or more, people take your offers more readily, and word sent above the usual wage brings more skilled people.
why.reputation.middle: At {high} or more, people take your offers more readily; at {low} or less, less readily, and fewer come asking.
why.reputation.low: At {low} or less, people take your offers less readily, and fewer come asking.

why.staffOutput.lesson: Hours alone don't make work: a rested, fairly paid worker with a happy home does more.

why.staffLongDays.lesson: More hours help for a few days; then tiredness eats the gain.

hand.lapse: The new season's wage couldn't be paid. They wait two days; renewing pays the whole season, the waiting days included.

why.pests.wet: Wet weather while it grows raises the risk.
why.pests.sprayed: You sprayed: the damage is limited.

why.garden.lesson: The kitchen garden feeds the family a little every day.

why.payback.title: Has it paid for itself?
why.payback.lesson: A tree costs now and pays for years: that's an investment.
why.sapling.title: {tree} sapling
why.sapling.planting: The price includes digging and planting it.
why.cash.title: Cash
why.cash.quiet: No money in or out yet today.
why.cash.lesson: Cash is not profit: paying ahead or buying stock moves cash without being a cost yet.
why.store.title: Your store
why.store.room: The hut holds a fixed weight. What doesn't fit waits where it is or sells to the trader.
why.store.lesson: Sell before the store fills, or a harvest has nowhere to go.
why.price.index: Prices this year (they rise a little each season)
why.traderPrice.title: What the trader pays for {good}
why.traderPrice.lesson: The trader buys at the valley's price less the carting, up to what he can take each day.
why.orderPrice.title: What the supermarket pays for {good}
why.orderPrice.lesson: A buyer who pays more wants something back: produce harvested today, the amount it asks for, by midnight.
why.owed.title: The supermarket owes you
why.owed.when: Booked as a sale when you delivered; the cash comes at 6:00.
why.owed.lesson: A sale isn't cash until it's paid. Money owed to you still counts in what you're worth.
why.truck.title: The trader's truck
why.truck.price: His price is set at 6:00 and holds all day.
why.truck.lesson: Sell in the morning and you know the price. Big harvests are what the store and the mandi are for.
why.marketPrice.title: {good} on the village market
why.marketPrice.floor: It never stays far below what the trader pays
why.marketPrice.ceiling: Or far above what bringing it in costs
why.marketPrice.offered: What's on offer, yours included, pushes the price down.
why.marketPrice.town: Your town buys about this much a day
why.marketPrice.demand: With nothing on offer, the price sits at the valley's.
why.marketPrice.lesson: Offer a little at a time: a glut sinks the price to the trader's.
why.traderRoom.title: The trader can still take
why.traderRoom.lesson: His room comes back each morning.
why.spoilage.title: Spoils by tomorrow
why.spoilage.offer: Stock you've offered at the market spoils last.
why.spoilage.lesson: Grain keeps; potatoes, fruit and greens don't. Sell the quick spoilers first.
why.input.title: {good} in store
why.input.use: It counts as a cost when you sow or spray with it.
why.input.lesson: Buying ahead swaps cash for stock: your profit isn't touched until you use it.
why.inputPrice.title: {good} costs
why.inputPrice.lesson: Seed is dearer at sowing time: buying ahead saves money.

why.mandi.0: At the town mandi your goods fetch the valley's price when the trolley gets back, {hours} hours after it leaves.
why.mandi.1: The commission agent keeps {pct} of the sale.
why.mandi.2: A tractor-trolley is hired for the trip; it carries up to {kg}.
why.mandi.3: Going takes half an hour of your day, once a day at most.
why.mandi.4: The village trader pays less, but at once and with no trip.
why.mandi.lesson: A trip pays when the load is big enough to cover the trolley.
why.netWorth.title: What you own minus what you owe
why.netWorth.book: In your books (land and goods at what they cost)
why.netWorth.lesson: Net worth grows when what you earn beats what you spend and owe.
why.credit.title: {lender}: you can borrow
why.credit.base: Lends anyone in the village up to
why.credit.land: Land you bought counts for ({pct} of its value)
why.credit.inherited: Your family's land can never be pledged.
why.credit.tooLow: Your score is below what this lender accepts.
why.credit.lesson: Borrow only for what earns more than the interest.

why.loan.bullet: Interest each season; the whole loan back with the last payment.
why.loan.instalments: A part of the loan back each season, with its interest.
why.loan.lesson: A missed payment costs late interest and your score.
why.borrow.title: Paying back over
why.borrow.lesson: A longer term means smaller payments but more interest in all.
why.calendar.title: The calendar
why.calendar.clock: The game's clock matches your phone's: the farm keeps working while the app is closed.
why.calendar.away: Away longer than {hours} hours, the farm waits for you.
why.calendar.lesson: One hour here is about a day in the valley.
why.forecast.title: How sure is this?
why.forecast.runs: Weather comes in runs: calm weather lasts, storms pass in an hour or two.
why.forecast.lesson: Plan on today's forecast; keep a margin for the days after.
why.saved.title: Saving
why.saved.when: The game saves every hour, a few seconds after your last tap, and when you leave the app.
why.saved.backups: It keeps backups, so a crash never costs more than an hour.
why.labour.title: Your work today
why.labour.lesson: Eat well and rest: a tired, hungry founder gets less done.

letter.listSubtitle: Every page so far, in the order it came
letter.welcome: My dear beta, the farm is yours now. Six acres by the river, the hut your grandfather built, and the well that never failed us. The fields have rested too long and the soil is tired, but it is honest: it gives back what you put in. You'll find seed potato, some wheat and lentils, and greens seed in the store, and a little money to begin. Start small.
letter.garden: By the door is the baadi, our kitchen garden. Radish, spinach, coriander: they grow in minutes and feed the house. Sow one bed now; by the time you've looked around, it will be ready.
letter.household: A farm runs on the people who work it, and you are the first. Choose how the house eats and how long you work: good food and rest let you do more, day after day. The house eats from the store first. Your grandfather kept wheat and lentils from his last harvest; if you'd rather sow them than eat them, switch 'eat from the store' off for now.
letter.firstPick: There: your first basket. Everything you pick goes to the store, where it waits for you. Greens don't keep long, so eat them or sell them soon.
letter.firstSale: The trader comes to the gate every day and buys at a fair, low price. That's money today. His truck comes every morning at 6:00 and leaves at midnight. Later you'll learn when it pays to wait, or to take a cart to the mandi in town.
letter.longCrop: Now something that takes longer. Potato does well in Spring on the well acres, and the seed is already in the store. It takes about 15 hours. Crops wait in the field when they're ready, but not forever: after three days they start to spoil.
letter.comeBack: That's a good first day. The farm keeps going while you're away: the crops grow, the house eats, the trader buys. Your {crop} will be ready {time}. Want a nudge when it's ready? Never at night.
letter.comeBack.on: That's a good first day. The farm keeps going while you're away: the crops grow, the house eats, the trader buys. Your {crop} will be ready {time}.
letter.firstReturn: Welcome back. Here's what happened while you were away. Tap Collect all to bring in what's ready.
letter.firstFieldHarvest: Your first field harvest. Tap the ? beside it to see what made it: the soil, the water, your care, the weather, the seed. The weakest of them holds the rest back.
letter.pest: Pests on one of your fields. Spray now and you'll save most of the crop; leave it and you'll lose some. Fields that grow the same crop again and again draw more pests.
letter.sellOrStore: Your store is filling up. Three ways to sell: the trader at the gate (today, at his price), the village market (a little at a time, at a better price), or a cart to the mandi (a full load, half a day away, after the cart's hire). Or keep it for a better season, if it keeps.
letter.seasonReport: Your first season is done. The report shows whether the farm paid for itself. Money you paid ahead for next season isn't a cost yet, so cash and profit tell different stories.
letter.labour: Your fields need more hands than yours. A labourer from the next village stays for one crop, till its harvest; a farm hand stays for the season but needs a hut to live in. A Hamlet begins with a hand's house.
letter.borrowing: Money is short for what you want to do next. The moneylender lends quickly, at a high price. The bank lends more, cheaper, if you can show land or a good season. Borrow only what the work will pay back.
letter.sick: You're unwell today and the fields will wait. Eat well, rest, and the chemist in the village has medicine.
letter.hamlet: Look at what you've built: six acres in good heart, a house for a hand, a season that paid its way. This isn't a homestead any more. It's a Hamlet, and you can keep cattle now: tap your cattle yard beside the house.
letter.firstOrders: A shop in the city buys fresh produce straight from farms. It pays more than the trader, but only for what you harvest today, delivered by midnight, and it pays the next morning.
letter.truckAway: The trader's truck comes at 6:00 and leaves at midnight, or when it's full. The stall closes at night too. Keep it in the store, or take a cart to the mandi.

notify.HouseBuilt.body: A home for a family on your land.

notify.HandRetired.body: Their hut may be free for a new hand.
notify.FamilyMovedIn.title: {name}'s family moved in
notify.FamilyMovedIn.body: A new family lives in your family house.
why.townHappiness.title: Your town's happiness
why.townHappiness.mean: The average over everyone: a bigger family counts for more.
why.townHappiness.lesson: Happy people stay; each family's card shows what would help.
why.employment.title: Work in town
why.employment.what: Adults with a job here: your hands. The others work outside, on about half the days.
why.employment.outside: Outside work pays a day, on average
why.employment.lesson: A job in town is steadier than outside work, so it makes families happier.
why.householdIncome.title: Income this season
why.householdIncome.remit: Half sent home to the family
why.householdIncome.lesson: A family's income sets everything else: food first, then the rest.
why.householdBudget.title: The season's budget
why.householdBudget.engel: Engel's law: the less a family earns for each person, the bigger the share it spends on food.
why.householdBudget.lesson: As incomes rise, food takes a smaller share and more is left for everything else.
why.householdSavings.title: Savings
why.householdSavings.first: In a short season, savings buy the food first.
why.householdSavings.lesson: Savings carry a family through a bad season.
why.householdRent.title: Rent
why.householdRent.hut: A hand's hut is part of the pay: no rent.
why.householdRent.inKind: The house is part of the hand's pay: no rent.
why.householdRent.how: Paid at each season's close, from the budget first, then from savings.
why.householdRent.leave: A family {n} seasons behind may move away: half do, at each close. They owe nothing when they go.
why.householdRent.lesson: Rent pays back what the house cost, season by season.
why.householdHappiness.title: Happiness
why.householdHappiness.weights: Weights: food and a home {a}, a safe living {b}, belonging {c}, getting on {d}.
why.householdHappiness.gate: Each layer counts fully only once the one below it is met to {gate}.
why.householdHappiness.leave: A family below {below} at {n} closes in a row may move away: half do, at each close.
why.householdHappiness.lesson: People need food and a home before anything else.
why.citizenAge.title: Age
why.citizenAge.season: People age a year each season ({n} at each season's close).
why.citizenAge.stages: Children till {adult}, adults till {elder}, then elders.
why.citizenAge.lesson: A season is 4 days, so children grow up within weeks of play.
why.citizenHealth.title: Health
why.citizenHealth.food: Health falls in a season without enough food and comes back when they eat well.
why.citizenHealth.later: Doctors and a clinic come later.
why.citizenJob.title: Work
why.citizenJob.outside: Outside work pays a day, on average
why.citizenJob.hire: When you hire labourers, your town's own come first.
why.businessArea.title: The area's grain a day
why.businessArea.people: People who'd bring their grain (your town {town})
why.businessArea.each: Grain a person brings a day
why.businessArea.hours: They come between 8:00 and 18:00, a little each hour.
why.businessArea.lost: Grain your mill can't grind that hour goes to the next village's chakki.
why.businessArea.lesson: A village chakki lives on the area's grinding, not on its owner's wheat.
why.businessFee.title: The next village's fee
why.businessFee.next: There's no chakki nearer: people carry their grain to the next village's, which charges this.
why.businessFee.most: Charge no more than this, or they keep going there
why.businessFee.lesson: Customers compare prices: a little dearer and they walk on.
why.businessTrader.title: {good} at the trader
why.businessTrader.day: He takes at most a day
why.businessWage.title: A {role}'s wage a season
why.businessWage.paid: Paid at the start of each season from the business's own cash.
why.businessWage.who: The best-skilled adult in your town without a job here takes it; if there's nobody, a worker comes daily from a neighbouring village.
why.businessWage.you: Run it yourself and there's no wage, but your hours there come off your farm.
why.businessOwn.title: Your wheat a day
why.businessOwn.price: The mill pays your farm today's trader price
why.businessOwn.books: It's a sale on your farm's books and stock on the mill's: each keeps its own books.
why.businessOwn.yields: A kilo of wheat gives 0.97 kg of atta and 0.03 kg of bran.
why.businessOwn.lesson: Turning your own harvest into something worth more is where processing pays.
why.businessWorker.title: Who works here
why.businessWorker.you: You run it: it's open only in your hours there, and those come off your farm work.
why.businessWorker.neighbour: Nobody in your town was free, so a worker comes daily from a neighbouring village.
why.businessWorker.town: One of your people works here: a job in town for their family.
why.businessWorker.townJob: A job at your business counts as a job in town.
why.businessHours.title: Open hours
why.businessHours.area: People bring their grain between 8:00 and 18:00: closed in those hours, theirs goes to the next village.
why.businessHours.worker: The worker works the hours you set. Hours past 8:00–18:00 are overtime, paid at time and a half as they're worked, and long days tire them.
why.businessHours.you: You're at the mill these hours, so they come off your farm work.
why.businessMarket.title: Wheat at the market
why.businessMarket.price: Wheat bought in costs the market's price with its transport: a little atta margin is left.
why.businessMarket.lesson: Milling bought wheat keeps the chakki busy but pays thinly.
why.businessCash.title: The mill's cash
why.businessCash.own: The mill's own money, apart from yours: what you put in, fees and sales in, wheat, power and wages out.
why.businessCash.flow: Cash isn't profit: the machine was paid for at once but wears out over years.
why.businessCash.lesson: A business can make a profit and still run short of cash.
why.books.title: {line}, {period}
why.books.fees: The area's grain ground: {area}, at your fee of {fee} a kg. The grain stays theirs: you're paid for the work.
why.books.sales: What the trader's truck and your feed room paid for the atta and bran made from {own} of wheat.
why.books.goods: What the wheat in the atta and bran sold cost. Your own wheat comes in at the market price (a sale on your farm's books); what isn't sold yet stays in stock.
why.books.margin: Fees and sales less the cost of the wheat sold. It has to pay the running costs.
why.books.wages: The {role}'s wage, paid upfront for the season. Run by you, there's no wage: your hours there come off your farm work.
why.books.power: {kg} ground, at {power} a kg for the motor.
why.books.repairs: {share} of the equipment's value a season, paid at the close.
why.books.depreciation: The building ({building} over {buildingLife} seasons) and the equipment ({equipment} over {equipmentLife} seasons) wear out a little each season. No cash moves: it was paid when you built.
why.books.interest: Interest on the overdraft and the business loan.
why.books.profit: The gross margin less the running costs: wages, power, repairs, wear and interest.
why.books.cashStart: The cash it had when the season began.
why.books.cashIn: Fees, sales and any cash you put in.
why.books.cashOut: Wheat, power, wages, repairs and any cash you took out.
why.books.cashEnd: Cash at the start, plus money in, less money out.
why.books.stock: Wheat, atta and bran in stock, at what they cost.
why.books.fixed: What the building and equipment cost, less their wear so far.
why.books.debts: The overdraft and the business loan.
why.books.capital: The cash you've put in, less what you've taken out.
why.books.kept: The profits it has made and kept, less any losses.
why.books.worth: What it owns less what it owes. Your net worth counts it at this, never below 0.
why.books.pnlLesson: A business keeps its own books: its profit is its own, apart from your farm's.
why.books.cashLesson: Cash is not profit: the building was paid for once in cash but wears out a little each season, and stock is cash waiting to be sold.
why.books.balanceLesson: What a business owns = what it owes + what's yours in it.
why.booksPlan.wait: After {n} full seasons, each line's average a season is set against the plan you made on founding day, with why they differ.
why.booksPlan.title: {line}, a season
why.booksPlan.actual: Actual: the average of the last {n} seasons
why.booksPlan.lesson: A plan is a guess at today's prices: checking it against what happened is how you plan better next time.
why.plan.cost.title: Building and machine
why.plan.cost: A small shed and a 10 HP stone chakki with its motor, at today's prices.
why.plan.fees.title: Grinding fees a season
why.plan.fees: The area's grain, about {area} a day for {days} days, ground at {fee}.
why.plan.sales.title: Atta and bran a season
why.plan.sales: Your {own} a day turned into atta and bran, sold to the trader at today's prices.
why.plan.wheat.title: Your wheat a season
why.plan.wheat: The mill buys your {own} a day at today's trader price: your farm sells it, the mill pays.
why.plan.power.title: Power a season
why.plan.repairs.title: Repairs a season
why.plan.repairs: About {share} of the machine's cost each season keeps the stones dressed and the belts whole.
why.plan.depreciation.title: Wear and tear a season
why.plan.depreciation: The shed lasts about 20 years and the chakki about 10: their cost is spread over their seasons.
why.plan.wage.title: The {role}'s wage
why.plan.wage: A season's wage, paid at the start of each season.
why.plan.profit.title: Profit a season
why.plan.profit: Fees and sales less wheat, power, repairs, wear and tear and the wage.
why.plan.cash.title: Cash to put in
why.plan.cash: The building and machine ({cost}), and a season's running cash: the wage, or run by you, the power and repairs; less a business loan if you take one ({loan}).
why.plan.payback.title: Payback
why.plan.payback: The building and machine's {cost} over a season's profit of {profit}.
why.plan.loan.title: A business loan
why.plan.loan: The co-op bank lends a business up to {ltv} of its building and machine ({cost}), paid back in equal parts over {seasons} seasons from the business's own cash, with interest. You guarantee it: if the business can't pay, it counts on your credit, and closing it makes what's still owed your loan.
why.plan.interest.title: Interest on the loan
why.plan.interest: {loan} borrowed at {rate} a season: the first season's interest. It falls as the loan is paid down.
why.planHours.title: Your hours, at a day labourer's pay
why.planHours.farm: Running it yourself saves the wage, but those hours come off your farm work: fields get less care, and you can't do day labour then. The profit above doesn't count them.
why.planHours.lesson: Your own time has a price too: compare the wage you save with what your hours would earn.
why.businessOverdraft.title: Overdraft used
why.businessOverdraft.limit: Its limit: {pct} of a season's running costs
why.businessOverdraft.rate: Interest a season on what's drawn
why.businessOverdraft.draws: When its cash can't pay for wheat, power, repairs, a wage or a loan payment, the bank pays and the overdraft grows; money coming in pays it off first.
why.businessOverdraft.past: Past the limit it stops buying wheat (grinding for the area goes on), and at the close a wage it can't pay goes unpaid: the worker leaves.
why.businessOverdraft.lesson: An overdraft carries a business through a short patch, at a price; it's no way to run one.
why.businessClose.toYou: Comes to you if you close now
why.businessClose.yourLoan: Becomes your loan if you close now
why.businessClose.stock: Its atta and bran go to the trader at today's price.
why.businessClose.sale: The building and equipment sell at {pct} of what they're still worth on its books: used machines fetch less.
why.businessClose.debts: Its overdraft and business loan are repaid first; what they can't cover becomes your co-op bank loan over {seasons} seasons, because you guaranteed it.
why.businessClose.worker: Its worker leaves, and the acre is free to farm again.
why.businessClose.lesson: Closing ends a business's losses, but rarely gets back what you put in.
why.plan.lesson: A plan is a guess: after 4 seasons the mill's card compares it with what really happened.
why.handHome.title: Lives in
why.handHome.remit: Of the wage, sent home to the family in {village}
why.handHome.house: The family house, part of the pay, worth a season
place.houseHint: Tap a lit acre: an empty field you own, or the labour quarters.
why.householdHome.title: Their home
why.householdHome.lesson: A crowded home makes a family less happy: another house helps.
research.shops: The shops would buy {good} a day
business.shortCash.bakery: Short of cash: it can't buy atta. Put cash in, or close it.
books.goods.bakery: Cost of the pav and rusk sold
books.why.noOwn.bakery: It baked nothing: no atta, no cash to buy it, or a mix of 0
why.businessPeople.title: People the shops serve
why.businessPeople.area: The village and the hamlets around it
why.businessPeople.shops: The village grocer and tea stall sell to all of them, so your townspeople buy through the shops too.
why.recipeShops.title: The shops would buy {good}
why.recipeShops.each: A person buys in a real day (about three weeks of life)
why.recipeShops.price: They pay the trader's price that morning
why.recipeShops.round: They collect at 6:00 each morning, with the trader's truck: what was made since the last round, up to this much.
why.recipeShops.lesson: Sales, not the oven, set what a bakery earns: make what's wanted.
why.recipeInput.title: {good} costs
why.recipeInput.trader: From a mill of yours, at the trader's price
why.recipeInput.market: Bought at the market, with its transport
why.recipeInput.yours: Your mill sends its atta to your bakery first, at the trader's price: a sale on the mill's books, stock on the bakery's.
why.recipeInput.noMill: With no mill of yours, the bakery buys its atta at the market's import price.
why.recipeInput.lesson: Owning each step of a chain keeps the margin in your hands.
why.recipeMade.title: {good} made today
why.recipeMade.rate: The oven takes at most this much a real hour
why.recipeMade.recipe.pav.bakery: 10 kg of atta with sugar, oil and yeast makes {batch} of pav.
why.recipeMade.recipe.rusk.bakery: Rusk is pav sliced and baked twice: 12 kg of pav makes {batch}. The pav it uses is baked again for the shops.
why.recipeMade.round: It bakes in the open hours until the mix is made; the count starts again after the 6:00 round.
why.recipeStock.title: {good} in stock
why.recipeStock.round: Waiting for the shops' round at 6:00.
why.recipeStock.fresh: It keeps only a day: what the shops don't take at 6:00 is thrown away.
why.recipeStock.keeps: It keeps for weeks: after the shops, the trader takes up to {kg} a day.
why.recipeStock.part: Some of it goes stale each day.
why.recipeMix.title: {good} a day
why.recipeMix.fresh: It keeps only a day: bake more than the shops buy and the rest is thrown away.
why.recipeMix.keeps: It keeps, so the trader takes what the shops don't, up to his amount.
why.recipeMix.lesson: Make what you can sell: waste is a cost too.
why.businessCash.own.bakery: The bakery's own money, apart from yours: what you put in and its sales in; atta, firewood, supplies and wages out.
why.businessHours.area.bakery: The baker bakes in these hours; the shops collect at 6:00 whatever was baked since the last round.
why.businessHours.you.bakery: You're at the bakery these hours, so they come off your farm work.
why.businessMarket.price.bakery: Atta your mill can't give is bought at the market's import price, with its transport.
why.businessMarket.lesson.bakery: Stop buying and the oven waits for your mill's atta: cheaper, but less is baked.
why.plan.cost.bakery: A bakery shed with a wood-fired oven and a dough mixer, at today's prices.
why.plan.sales.bakery: What the village shops buy each morning, and the trader's rusk, for {days} days at today's prices. Bread they don't buy isn't counted.
why.plan.wheat.bakery: About {own} baked a day: its atta at what it costs today (your mill's at the trader's price, else the market's), and {supplies} of sugar, oil and yeast a {batch} batch.
why.plan.power.bakery: Each {batch} batch takes about {fuel} of firewood; rusk is baked again, so it takes more.
why.plan.repairs.bakery: About {share} of the oven and mixer's cost each season keeps the oven's bricks sound and the mixer turning.
why.plan.depreciation.bakery: The shed lasts about 20 years and the oven and mixer about 10: their cost is spread over their seasons.
why.plan.profit.bakery: Sales less atta, supplies, firewood, repairs, wear and tear and the wage.
why.plan.cash.bakery: The building and oven ({cost}), and a season's running cash: the wage, or run by you, the firewood and repairs; less a business loan if you take one ({loan}).
why.plan.lesson.bakery: A plan is a guess: after 4 seasons the bakery's card compares it with what really happened.
why.books.sales.bakery: What the village shops and the trader paid for the pav and rusk.
why.books.goods.bakery: What the atta and supplies in the bread sold cost, and bread thrown away unsold. Your mill's atta comes in at the trader's price.
why.books.margin.bakery: Sales less the cost of what was sold. It has to pay the running costs.
why.books.cashIn.bakery: Sales and any cash you put in.
why.books.cashOut.bakery: Atta, supplies, firewood, wages, repairs and any cash you took out.
why.books.stock.bakery: Atta, pav and rusk in stock, at what they cost.
why.businessOverdraft.draws.bakery: When its cash can't pay for atta, firewood, repairs, a wage or a loan payment, the bank pays and the overdraft grows; money coming in pays it off first.
why.businessOverdraft.past.bakery: Past the limit it can't buy atta, so the oven stops; at the close a wage it can't pay goes unpaid: the worker leaves.
why.businessClose.stock.bakery: Its atta, pav and rusk go to the trader at today's price.
research.traderTakes: The trader would take {good} a day
business.shortCash.dairy: Short of cash: it can't buy milk. Put cash in, or close it.
books.goods.dairy: Cost of the paneer, curd and ghee sold
books.why.noOwn.dairy: It made nothing: no milk kept, no cash to buy it, or a mix of 0
shed.milkTodayValueDairy: {milk} · {amount} from the co-op and your dairy at 6:00
shed.toYourDairy: Your dairy keeps up to {milk} a day at the co-op's price; the rest goes to the co-op
why.dairyMilk.title: Your {kind} milk a day
why.dairyMilk.price: The co-op's price this morning, a litre
why.dairyMilk.herd: What your milking animals give in a real day, less what your house drinks.
why.dairyMilk.books: Your dairy pays your farm the co-op's price for it: a sale on the farm's books, stock on the dairy's. Milk it doesn't keep still goes to the co-op.
why.dairyMilk.lesson: Your own milk is your dairy's cheapest: no premium, no carting.
why.dairyNeighbours.title: Neighbours' milk
why.dairyNeighbours.coop: The co-op's price for buffalo milk
why.dairyNeighbours.premium: What your dairy pays above it
why.dairyNeighbours.why: Neighbours sell to your dairy at 6:00 only if it pays a little more than the co-op; it fills the milk a day after your own.
why.dairyNeighbours.lesson: A village dairy runs on the village's milk: a herd of four can't keep it busy.
why.dairyMilkADay.title: Milk a day
why.dairyMilkADay.herd: Your herd gives, less the house's
why.dairyMilkADay.neighbours: It keeps your milk first at 6:00, then buys neighbours' milk up to this much.
why.dairyMilkADay.yoursOnly: It keeps only your milk, up to this much: you've stopped buying neighbours'.
why.dairyMilkADay.spoils: Milk not made up by the next milking spoils, so keep only what the mix needs.
why.recipeMade.rate.dairy: The dairy handles at most this much milk a real hour
why.recipeMade.recipe.paneer.dairy: 5 litres of buffalo milk make a kilo of paneer (cow milk, about a third more): {batch} a batch, split with lemon and pressed.
why.recipeMade.recipe.curd.dairy: A litre of milk sets into a kilo of curd overnight: {batch} a batch.
why.recipeMade.recipe.ghee.dairy: 15 litres of buffalo milk (22 of cow's) give a kilo of ghee: the cream churned to butter and boiled down.
why.recipeShops.lesson.dairy: Paneer and curd sell only fresh: make what the shops take, and ghee, which keeps, for the trader.
why.businessCash.own.dairy: The dairy's own money, apart from yours: what you put in and its sales in; milk, fuel and wages out.
why.businessHours.area.dairy: The dairyman works the morning's milk in these hours; the shops collect at 6:00 what was made since the last round.
why.businessHours.you.dairy: You're at the dairy these hours, so they come off your farm work.
why.businessMarket.price.dairy: After your own milk, the dairy buys neighbours' milk at 6:00 up to its milk a day, at the co-op's price and a little more.
why.businessMarket.lesson.dairy: Stop buying and it works only your herd's milk: less made, but only your own margin.
why.plan.cost.dairy: A dairy room with a cream separator, a kadhai and burner, a paneer press and a chest freezer, at today's prices.
why.plan.sales.title.dairy: Paneer, curd and ghee a season
why.plan.sales.dairy: What the village shops buy each morning, and the trader's ghee, for {days} days at today's prices, as far as the milk goes.
why.plan.wheat.dairy: About {own} made a day from the milk it keeps: your herd's at the co-op's price, then neighbours' at a little more.
why.plan.power.dairy: Gas for the kadhai, and lemon and culture: about {fuel} a batch.
why.plan.repairs.dairy: About {share} of the equipment's cost each season keeps the separator and freezer running.
why.plan.depreciation.dairy: The room lasts about 20 years and the equipment about 10: their cost is spread over their seasons.
why.plan.profit.dairy: Sales less milk, fuel, repairs, wear and tear and the wage.
why.plan.cash.dairy: The room and equipment ({cost}), and a season's running cash: the wage, or run by you, the fuel and repairs; less a business loan if you take one ({loan}).
why.plan.lesson.dairy: A plan is a guess: after 4 seasons the dairy's card compares it with what really happened.
why.books.sales.dairy: What the village shops and the trader paid for the paneer, curd and ghee.
why.books.goods.dairy: What the milk in what was sold cost, and milk, paneer and curd thrown away unsold. Your own milk comes in at the co-op's price.
why.books.margin.dairy: Sales less the cost of what was sold. It has to pay the running costs.
why.books.cashIn.dairy: Sales and any cash you put in.
why.books.cashOut.dairy: Milk, fuel, wages, repairs and any cash you took out.
why.books.stock.dairy: Milk, paneer, curd and ghee in stock, at what they cost.
why.businessOverdraft.draws.dairy: When its cash can't pay for milk, fuel, repairs, a wage or a loan payment, the bank pays and the overdraft grows; money coming in pays it off first.
why.businessOverdraft.past.dairy: Past the limit it can't pay for milk, so the co-op takes it all; at the close a wage it can't pay goes unpaid: the worker leaves.
why.businessClose.stock.dairy: Its ghee goes to the trader at today's price; fresh stock is sold off with it.
why.recipeMix.loses: At today's prices it costs {cost} a kilo to make and fetches {price}: it loses, so it isn't in the starting mix.
reject.AlreadyStaffed: Someone already works there. Let them go first.
board.title: Hiring board
board.subtitle: Send word for a job, then choose who to hire.
board.handWhere: Works your fields and takes your orders; lives in a hut or their own home
board.letGoOnCard: Let go from the business's card
board.youRunIt: You run it yourself. Hire someone and your hours go back to the farm.
board.postMarketWhy: Your townspeople hear at once; others come for 4 days
board.postAboveWhy: Better, surer people; they ask 10% more
board.handNeedsHome: Someone from outside needs an empty hut. Your townspeople don't.
board.postFirst: Send word, and people will ask
board.referenceWhy: Their last employer tells you their skill, and how they left
board.fromTown: From your town: you know them well
board.regular: Worked your fields as a labourer
board.commutes: Would come daily from a neighbouring village
board.offerSubtitle: A season's contract as your {role}, paid upfront.
board.counterNote: Offer this and they'll take it
board.noteAsked: A fair wage for their skill
board.noteLow: Saves money now, but they remember it and work less gladly
board.noteHigh: Surer, and they start out glad of it
board.houseInPay: From next season: {cash} in cash + the house (worth {house})
board.houseInOthersPay: The house is already part of {name}'s pay: all of this is cash
business.runYourselfWhy: No wage, but its hours come off your farm work
business.needsWorker: Nobody works here: hire someone on the board, or run it yourself.
why.jobUsual.title: A {role}'s usual wage
why.jobUsual.hand: What a farm hand of middling skill (50) is paid a season in the villages round here, at today's prices.
why.jobUsual.business: What this work pays a person of middling skill (50) a season round here, at today's prices.
why.jobUsual.farming: The job uses their farming skill.
why.jobUsual.crafting: The job uses their crafting skill: a careful hand at a machine or an oven.
why.jobUsual.skill: Each person asks more or less by their skill: from a fifth less for a beginner to a fifth more for an expert.
why.jobWage.title: What {name} asks
why.jobWage.usual: The usual wage for the job
why.jobWage.skill: They ask more the more skilled they are: a fifth less at skill 0, a fifth more at skill 100.
why.jobWage.above: You sent word above the usual wage, so they ask 10% more.
why.jobWage.town: They live in your town: they take what they ask or more, and often a little less.
why.jobWage.migrant: They don't know you yet: most take what they ask, fewer take less.
why.jobWage.low: Offer 10% less and they may refuse. If they do, they'll ask once for their wage instead. Hired low, they remember it until a new season pays what they ask.
why.jobWage.high: Offer 10% more and they're surer to say yes, and start out glad of it.
why.jobWage.lesson: Paying below the market saves money now and often costs more later.
why.jobReference.title: Asking their last employer
why.jobReference.what: For a small fee, their last employer tells you their skill more closely, within a few points. It takes half a day.
why.jobReference.terms: "Was let go" usually means a lazy or careless worker.
why.jobReference.lesson: Hiring is a guess. A reference makes it a better one.
ledger.reference: A reference asked about an applicant
event.CourseFinished: A worker came back from a course.
event.LongDaysStopped: Long days stopped: the overtime couldn't be paid.
event.CounterOffer: They asked for their wage instead.
event.WorkerHired: A worker started at your business.
